---
title: "DuckDB CLI"
jupyter: coi-docs
---

No install beyond the [`duckdb`](https://duckdb.org/docs/installation/)
binary itself — no Python, no R, no account.

## Attach and query

```sh
duckdb -c "
ATTACH 'https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/cancerbasemap.duckdb' AS cbm (READ_ONLY);
SELECT source, count(*) AS rows FROM cbm.measure.observation GROUP BY source ORDER BY source;
"
```

This page's own output is the real thing — run at build time, through the
actual `duckdb` binary, not typed in by hand:

```{python}
#| echo: false
import subprocess

sql = """
ATTACH 'https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/cancerbasemap.duckdb' AS cbm (READ_ONLY);
SELECT source, count(*) AS rows FROM cbm.measure.observation GROUP BY source ORDER BY source;
"""
result = subprocess.run(["duckdb", "-c", sql], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
print(result.stdout)
```

Drop `-c "..."` for an interactive shell (`duckdb`), then paste the `ATTACH`
once per session and query freely — `cbm` stays attached for the rest of that
shell. Replace `latest` with a dated folder such as `v2026-11-02` to pin a
release.

Piping to a file works the same as any other DuckDB output:

```sh
duckdb -c "ATTACH 'https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/cancerbasemap.duckdb' AS cbm (READ_ONLY); COPY (SELECT * FROM cbm.measure.definition) TO 'measures.csv';"
```

Every release also ships a `views.sql` (the same views, created in your own
session) and plain Parquet files. `.read` cannot open a URL, so download it
first:

```sh
curl -sO https://basemap.cancerdatasci.org/data/latest/views.sql
duckdb -c ".read views.sql" -c "SELECT count(*) FROM geography.unit"
```
